newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen says to fight Krupp bid.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen says to fight Krupp bid.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Thyssen AG said on Tuesday it would seek partners to fight off a hostile takeover bid by rival Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp.
Thyssen said the bid puts it in a serious situation, but that management and labour would fight to secure Thyssen's future.
Any bidder would need eight to nine billion marks in capital, Thyssen said.
Thyssen says to fight Krupp bid

"It cannot lead to sensible results, to destroy a strong, healthy company, well prepared for the future, to solve the possible problems of another company or to satisfy the short-term profit interests of capital providers," Thyssen said in a statement signed by management board chairman Dieter Vogel, supervisory board chairman Heinz Kriwet and works council head Georg Bongen.
Tens of thousands of Thyssen and Krupp jobs hang in the balance, the Thyssen statement said.

To assure investors of an adequate return on an eight to nine billion marks ($4.7-$5.3 billion) takeover bid, a buyer would have to consume all of Thyssen's capital reserves and make deep rationalisation cuts, it said.

"This has nothing to do with a planned, responsible management strategy that is equally oriented toward the workers' interests as well as capital," it said. "These are Wild West methods that are incomprehensible in view of the current problems in Germany and in North Rhine-Westphalia."
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.690 German Marks)
